title: Priorities, Deadlines & Workload
summary: Learn how to identify priorities, understand deadlines, recognize workload limits, and clarify competing expectations before they become missed commitments.
objectives: Recognize when competing priorities require clarification.
Identify when workload exceeds available time or capacity.

vocab.def: The relative importance or order in which work should receive attention.
The time by which an assigned task or result is expected.
The amount of work a person or team is responsible for during a period of time.
The realistic amount of work that can be completed with available time and resources.

sections.heading: Not every task has the same priority
sections.body: Some work is urgent, some is important but not urgent, and some can wait. Strong workers understand the difference instead of treating every request as equally immediate.

sections.heading: Deadlines affect connected work
sections.body: A missed deadline may affect customers, teammates, approvals, meetings, deliveries, or other tasks that depend on your work.

sections.heading: Competing priorities should be clarified
sections.body: If two supervisors, customers, or assignments appear to require attention at the same time, do not silently guess which one matters more. Clarify the priority with the appropriate person.

sections.heading: Capacity is a real constraint
sections.body: Accepting more work than can realistically be completed can create missed deadlines and lower quality. Recognizing capacity early allows time to adjust expectations or ask for help.

practice.prompt: You have two assignments due today and cannot finish both on time. What should you do?
practice.answer: Communicate early, explain the conflict accurately, and clarify priority or available options.

practice.prompt: A task is important but not due for several days, while another task is due in one hour. Does that automatically mean the one-hour task should always come first?
practice.answer: Not automatically. Deadline is one factor; safety, impact, instructions, dependencies, and organizational priority may also matter.

quiz.question: What is the strongest response to conflicting workplace priorities?
options: Clarify the priority and communicate the workload conflict
Promise both will be finished even when that is unrealistic
quiz.answer: Clarify the priority and communicate the workload conflict

lab.objective: Review a simulated workload containing deadlines, dependencies, and competing requests, then create a justified priority order.

reflectionPrompt: Why can asking for priority clarification be more responsible than trying to do everything at once?
